evidence.correctness: Ran the 10 unittest tests (OK, 0.19 s) and experiments/run.py (11.6 s; output byte-identical to the committed results.txt). Recomputed independently with my own numpy script (scratchpad/interference/indep.py): radar-equation clear range r0(s0/T)^(1/4)=158.114 m; E[1/d^2] for d^2~U[25,40000] = ln(1600)/39975 = 1.84559e-4 (also checked by quadrature), mean interference Kqc E[1/d^2]=36.912, mean-rise ranges 92.92/75.29/63.72/53.76/45.28 m for q=0.02..0.4, all exact matches. K=1 closed form at 80 m q=0.2 by hand 0.82468 (results.txt 0.8247). K=4 marginal Pd by a binomial mixture over the number of hits with 3e6-sample convolution of c/d^2 (a different method than the author's 4000-geometry subset enumeration): Pd(40,60,80,100)=0.9787/0.8866/0.6922/0.6561 vs 0.978/0.889/0.694/0.656; Pd(63.72)=0.857 vs 0.858; r90 at q=0.02..0.4 = 158.11/70.08/58.11/48.35/40.30 vs 158.11/70.19/58.39/48.52/40.39 (author's values within ~0.3 m, MC noise from 4000 geometries, never reported). Binomial tails P(>=9/10|0.98)=0.9838, P(>=3/10|0.656)=0.9957, P(>=9/10|0.656)=0.0921 match the table. One wrong reported output: 'real per-frame Pd at the clear-air range 158.1 m: 0.000' is a floating-point artefact (echo_power(clear_range) = 9.999999999999993 < T); in exact arithmetic at r=rc a clean frame (prob 0.9^4=0.6561) still detects, and just below rc Pd=0.6561. Core math correct; the boundary statement is wrong.

evidence.verification: 10 tests pass (unittest and PYTHONPATH=src pytest). Seeded 7 mutations in model.py, each reverted with git checkout: caught 4 (p*=1-q -> 1-q*q; log(R^2/d0^2) -> log(R/d0); binom_tail range m -> m+1; mean-rise exponent 0.25 -> 0.5). SURVIVED 3: (a) mean_interference drops q (K*q*c -> K*c), the headline 36.9 and every mean-rise range then wrong, all tests green because the only test of it uses mean_interference itself; (b) pd_given_geometry SINR rule S>=T(1+I) -> S>=T(1+0.5I) at model.py:82, the function behind results (2)-(4), green because its only consistency test is at 100 m where both versions give p_ok=0; (c) mission_success_fixed m -> m-1, green (only a monotonicity test). Survival 3/7. No test pins results.txt numbers or any K=4 value.
evidence.craft: Read model.py (113 lines), run.py, figure.py, tests. Small, stdlib-only, docstrings state the model, closed forms sensibly separated from MC. Defects: hard >= threshold evaluated at an exact float boundary (the Pd=0 artefact); `import random` unused in model.py:7; draw_geometry's comprehension names 1/d^2 `c_inv` (model.py:38), misleading; range_at_pd returns lo when pd(lo)<target, conflating 'no range' with r=1 m; Brier for geom_blind/iid is scored on the same test geometries the forecast averages over (in-sample, tiny bias at n=6000); no seeds/SE reported; pyproject has no test config. Nothing a reviewer would reject outright.
evidence.claims: Every README number matches results.txt. Wrong claim: README:3 'the clear-air twin's 158 m is reached with Pd 0' and whitepaper:12 'clear-air twin range 158.1 m has real Pd 0' - a float artefact; the same README sentence then says clean frames are detected 'out to 158 m', contradicting itself, and results.txt prints Pd>=0.5 range 158.11 next to Pd(158.1)=0.000. Unbacked precision: ranges given to 0.01 m and '9% optimistic' from a 4000-geometry MC with no interval (independent r90 is 58.11 vs 58.39). Disclosure of 'Stylised' and 'c and q illustrative' is honest but is the pattern research/CLAUDE.md ('Run the numbers; don't stylise them') says to avoid: q is derivable from chirp duty cycle and c from a radar datasheet, and no sweep over c or K is shown. Novelty is implied (title frames the mean-rise twin as an open question) without citing the stochastic-geometry literature where outage vs mean interference is standard.
evidence.fitness: Nearest prior work: stochastic-geometry analysis of automotive radar interference (Al-Hourani et al., 'Stochastic geometry methods for modeling automotive radar interference', IEEE T-ITS 2018; Munari et al., 'Stochastic geometry interference analysis of radar network performance', IEEE Commun. Lett. 2018), which gives detection/success probability as the Laplace transform of the interference rather than a mean noise rise; finite binomial point processes (Srinivasa & Haenggi 2010); and temporal correlation of interference across slots under fixed geometry with ALOHA-style activity (Ganti & Haenggi 2009; Haenggi & Ganti, 'Interference in Large Wireless Networks', 2009), which is exactly result (3). Brooker 2007 (IEEE TEMC) and Goppelt 2010 give q from chirp timing. That 'mean interference as noise' misstates outage, that Pd floors at P(no hit), and that fixed geometry correlates frame failures are known results; only the twin framing is new. No real radar parameters, no measurements, single (c,K) point. A researcher would start from the stochastic-geometry papers, not this.
evidence.domain: Physics shape is right (two-way 1/r^4 echo, one-way 1/d^2 interference, hit-or-miss chirp overlap, uniform-area placement). A radar engineer would depart on: q not derived from chirp duration/slope/frame time; no antenna pattern or field-of-view (most robot radars are directional, so the main-lobe alignment probability dominates); hard SINR threshold instead of a Swerling/Albersheim Pd-SNR curve; no interference mitigation (blanking/zeroing is standard in production FMCW chips); fixed K instead of a density sweep. Method is sound textbook probability, not a field-grade model.

verdict: Below the bar. The probability is correct: every closed form (clear range, E[1/d^2], mean-rise ranges, K=1 Pd, binomial tails) matched my independent recomputation exactly, and an independent 3e6-sample mixture reproduced the K=4 Pd curve within MC noise. But one reported output is a float artefact turned into a stated finding (Pd 0 at the clear-air range; the true value is 0.656), 3 of 7 seeded mutations in core logic survive (including the detection rule behind results 2-4 and the q in the headline mean interference), and as research it restates known stochastic-geometry results (outage is not set by mean interference; fixed geometry correlates frame failures) without citing that literature, with invented c and q and a single (c,K) point. Median score 2; claims and verification both below 3.
